steps: 'Drip and suck': NBM, IV fluids + electrolyte correction, nasogastric decompression.
CT to identify cause/level and detect ischaemia/strangulation.
Strangulation, closed-loop, ischaemia or perforation → urgent surgery.
Adhesional small-bowel obstruction without ischaemia: trial of conservative management.
Analgesia, antiemetics, urinary catheter; surgical review for all.

drugRefs.dose: ~1 L over the first hour, then titrated to deficit/urine output
drugRefs.freq: continuous, with correction of K⁺/Cl⁻ losses
drugRefs.why: Replaces fluid/electrolyte losses from vomiting and third-spacing into the obstructed bowel.
Controls colicky/visceral pain; titrate carefully and reassess for developing peritonism.

drugRefs.freq: up to three times daily as needed
drugRefs.why: Controls vomiting; prokinetic antiemetics are avoided in mechanical obstruction.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Acute Intestinal Obstruction
WSES Bologna Guidelines for Adhesive Small Bowel Obstruction
ACS Surgical Guidance — Management of Bowel Obstruction

decision.label: Drip and suck; urgent surgery if strangulation/ischaemia

confirm: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distension, absolute constipation; imaging (AXR/CT) confirms level and cause.
